title: {{NAME}} and the Roar That Shook the Crystal Tower
moral: True courage means standing up for others even when your knees are trembling.

pages.content:
Beyond the Whispering Mountains, where the sky glowed the colour of ripe peaches, stood the Crystal Tower of Princess Seraphina. Its walls caught every beam of sunlight and scattered them into a thousand rainbows across the valley below. {{NAME}} had travelled three days on the back of a friendly Triceratops named Bouldertoe just to reach this place. Bouldertoe's three horns gleamed like polished ivory, and his footsteps made the ground hum like a deep, satisfied drum. The valley smelled of pine needles and something else, something electric and strange, like a storm deciding whether to arrive.

Then {{NAME}} heard it. A sound like the whole world cracking open. From behind the tower rose a shadow so enormous it swallowed three rainbows at once. It was Grimscale, the ancient rogue T-Rex, his amber eyes blazing with mischief rather than malice, but his massive tail already sweeping through the tower's lower gardens, scattering the princess's prized midnight roses.

{{NAME}} pressed both hands to the sides of the superhero cape, feeling the cool fabric snap in the breeze. Seraphina appeared at the tower's highest window, her silver crown slightly crooked, her expression not frightened but furious. She pointed directly at Grimscale and then, surprisingly, directly at {{NAME}}. She needed a partner, not a rescuer. That was a very different thing.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} slid off Bouldertoe's broad back and sprinted to the tower door, heart hammering like a woodpecker on an oak. Up the spiralling staircase, two steps at a time, past portraits of ancient dinosaur knights and tapestries woven with superhero crests, until at last the door at the top burst open and there was Seraphina.

She was taller than {{NAME}} expected, with sharp dark eyes and ink-stained fingers that suggested she spent more time reading battle plans than brushing her crown. She thrust a rolled parchment into {{NAME}}'s hands. 'Grimscale is not evil,' she said, the words tumbling out fast and certain. 'He is lonely. His herd left him behind when the northern glacier melted. He destroys things because he does not know how to ask for company.'

{{NAME}}'s eyebrows climbed toward the ceiling. A lonely T-Rex. A princess who did her research. This was not the rescue story {{NAME}} had expected to be part of, and somehow that made it far more interesting. Outside, another thunderous crash shook the tower, and a small shower of crystal shards tinkled to the floor like broken music.

pages.content:
The plan was Seraphina's. The execution belonged to {{NAME}}, Bouldertoe, and every ounce of the courage that cape had ever promised to hold.

{{NAME}} charged back outside and positioned at the base of the Crystal Tower, cape billowing like a royal flag in a gale. 'GRIMSCALE!' The shout tore across the valley, surprisingly large for such a small person. The T-Rex froze, one enormous foot hovering mid-step, amber eyes swinging downward. Bouldertoe planted his three horns wide and let out a long, low rumble, the kind that meant friendship in old dinosaur language. Seraphina flung open the tower's great doors and rolled out an enormous feast she had been preparing for a week, roasted ferns and giant honeycomb and a mountain of warm volcanic bread, all smelling impossible and wonderful.

Grimscale blinked. His jaw unclenched. A sound came from deep in his chest, not a roar, something softer and bewildered, like a question. His great tail stilled. He lowered his enormous head until his snout was level with {{NAME}}'s nose, close enough that his warm breath ruffled the gold stars on the cape. {{NAME}} did not step back. Not even one centimetre.

pages.content:
For a long, stretched moment everything was still. The valley held its breath. Even the scattered rainbows seemed to pause.

Then Grimscale made his choice. He sat. A creature the size of a castle, simply sitting, like a dog who has finally found the right hearth. The ground shuddered with tremendous gentleness. His tail curled around the base of the tower, not crushing it, protecting it, the way a cat curls around something precious in the cold.

Seraphina walked to him without hesitation and placed one small, ink-stained hand against his jaw. 'You are not forgotten,' she told him, quiet and steady. 'You are here now.' Grimscale closed his amber eyes. The sound that rose from him then was low and rhythmic, almost like a purr, almost like a lullaby, something {{NAME}} felt more in the chest than heard with the ears. Bouldertoe pressed his broad side against {{NAME}}'s hip in the warm way that means everything is alright. {{NAME}}'s legs, which had been trembling for the last ten minutes without permission, finally decided to stop.

pages.content:
That evening, the four of them shared Seraphina's feast beneath the stars. The volcanic bread was extraordinary, warm and smoky and tasting faintly of adventure. Grimscale ate most of the roasted ferns and then tucked his chin onto his forelimbs with a sigh that sent a gentle breeze through everyone's hair. Bouldertoe fell asleep standing up, snoring softly through all three nostrils.

Seraphina poured starberry juice into two small cups and handed one to {{NAME}}. 'You didn't flinch,' she said, with an approving tilt of her head. {{NAME}} thought about that. The truth was the flinch had been there, fizzing and urgent, right behind the knees. But it had not won.

{{NAME}} lay back on the soft grass and watched the stars multiply overhead, a cape spread wide like wings. Tomorrow Grimscale would help rebuild the midnight rose garden, which was Seraphina's idea and a very good one. Tomorrow Bouldertoe would teach Grimscale the old low rumble of greeting. Tomorrow the valley would be something new.

But right now, sweet one, let your eyes grow heavy just like {{NAME}}'s are doing. Sleep is coming on gentle paws. And somewhere in the dark, there is a tiny blue egg at the top of the Crystal Tower that nobody noticed until tonight, and it is beginning, very softly, to glow.
